name: OpenVibe.Bot
tagline: Get your robot online in minutes.
description: OpenVibe.Bot is an open control panel for robots. Add a robot, pair it with one command on the robot (or a QR code for a phone), and drive it from any browser with live video, real controls and a stop button that always works. It runs a Raspberry Pi robot such as the Adeept 4WD kit, a ROS 2 robot, a Cozmo, a LOOI or a phone, and anything else through the generic relay and your own script. Share control, automate it, hand it to your AI agent, and show it on OpenVibe.Live or openre.stream when you want to.

pillars.title: Pair devices
pillars.text: Revocable device keys and one-time pairing codes, not stream keys.

pillars.title: Share control
pillars.text: Owner, whitelist, queues, timed turns, moderators and apps.

pillars.title: Safe on the device
pillars.text: Dead-man stop, command limits and local emergency stop.

pillars.title: Stream it
pillars.text: Show the camera on a Live channel, or embed a read-only view in any website.

faq.question: Do I need to open ports on my router?
faq.answer: No. The robot connects out to OpenVibe, and video and controls travel over WebRTC, so it works behind ordinary home and mobile networks.

faq.question: Is it only for streaming?
faq.answer: No. Streaming is optional. Bot is a control panel for your robot first: drive it, check on it, share it and automate it.

faq.question: Which robots have built-in support?
faq.answer: The Adeept 4WD Smart Car Kit for Raspberry Pi (ordinary or mecanum wheels), ROS 2 robots that take cmd_vel, Cozmo, LOOI through the community's Bluetooth bridge, and a phone, whose browser becomes the robot. OpenVibe's device agent drives each one directly, so no robot's own control port is ever exposed.

faq.question: Does it work with Cozmo?
faq.answer: Yes, built in. Cozmo makes its own Wi-Fi and runs closed firmware, so the OpenVibe agent runs on a computer next to it (a Raspberry Pi or a laptop) that joins Cozmo's Wi-Fi and stays online through another connection. You get driving, the head and lift, its camera, its face display, its voice, lights and cubes, and it stops at edges on its own. No phone app needed.

faq.question: What hardware works?
faq.answer: A Raspberry Pi or another Linux board running the OpenVibe Node, with a driver for your model; a ROS 2 robot; a Cozmo or a LOOI through a computer next to it; or any phone, in its browser, with nothing to install. Anything else joins through the generic relay and your own script, or a driver you write and submit for others to use. The Adeept kit's page lists its parts; OpenVibe does not sell hardware.

faq.question: How does it keep the robot safe?
faq.answer: The device stops its motors by itself when commands or the connection stop. There is an emergency stop in the panel, limits on speed, range and time, and every command is logged.

faq.question: What will it cost?
faq.answer: Controlling your own robot is free. Any paid extra would be listed on the site, with its price, before it starts.
